DATA NOTE: Today's bundle zip (2026-08-02) was unavailable at publication time; this brief draws on the 2026-08-01 lake data, the most recent complete dataset, supplemented by 10 live WebSearch queries executed this morning. Live items from Ukrainska Pravda and other feeds show coverage extending into 02 August UTC.

Headline

Three arcs defined the last 24 hours. Ukraine simultaneously absorbed its most destructive ballistic missile barrage in weeks and delivered its deepest long-range strike package of the summer, hitting three Bashneft refineries in Ufa, 1,600 km from the front, and sinking a Fesco/Rosatom container ship in the Black Sea. The Israel-Iran ceasefire is holding at 78% on Polymarket through 02 August but is priced at only 70% through 03 August, a structured daily step-down that the markets read as residual fracture risk. In Moscow, a targeted bombing outside a restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square killed three people, including the suspected bomber, and injured 21 others; the event was connected in open-source reporting to a private birthday gathering for the commander of the Russian Aerospace Forces, General Alexander Chaiko. Watch areas Israel-Iran-Hezbollah axis and Russia oil sanctions perimeter both fired today.

Macro situation

The US yield curvefred.stlouisfed.org ended July with a +47 bp 10Y-2Y spread, the most positive reading since the brief uninversion of Q1 2025. The curve's shape is now a textbook bear steepener: the front end is anchored by the Fed funds effective rate at 3.63%fred.stlouisfed.org, reflecting 275 bp of cumulative cuts since the 2024 peak, while the long end drifts upward under fiscal pressure. The 30-year Treasuryfred.stlouisfed.org at 5.21% is now 158 basis points above the 2-year, the steepest long-to-short spread since 2015. This matters because the 30-year is the reference rate for 30-year fixed mortgages and long-duration pension liabilities, and any further rise presses hard on both housing affordability and corporate defined-benefit plans. [medium]

The 10-yearfred.stlouisfed.org at 4.68% sits approximately 46 bp above the Fed funds rate. That spread is historically narrow by bear-steepener standards. In previous steepening cycles following rate-cut campaigns (1995, 2001, 2009), the 10Y-FF spread often reached 100-150 bp before the economy absorbed the rate reduction. The current compression implies the market does not yet price a strong recovery premium or a meaningful term premium re-rating, which in turn suggests the consensus view is still soft-landing-adjacent rather than reflation. [medium]

Anomaly

The one genuine anomaly this week is JPY/USD at 163.71, clocking +2.1 sigma above the 90-day mean. The yen has been the single most structurally distorted G10 currency since the Bank of Japan's yield-curve-control era, and the current level reflects both the 325 bp carry differential against the US and the BOJ's reluctance to accelerate normalization in the face of wavering domestic demand. A daily SOFRfred.stlouisfed.org rate of 3.65% matches overnight markets well. VIXfred.stlouisfed.org at 17.09 is near 12-month median; the equity volatility surface is not pricing a major risk event in the near term.

Core PCEfred.stlouisfed.org remains at 130.266 (June reading), consistent with inflation slightly above the 2% target but decelerating. Unemploymentfred.stlouisfed.org at 4.2% is creeping upward from 2024 lows; nonfarm payrollsfred.stlouisfed.org stand at 158,984 thousand as of June. The July employment report drops 07 August; consensus expects +130,000 and an unchanged 4.2% rate. A miss below +80,000 would reignite September cut speculation.

WTI crudefred.stlouisfed.org at $84.25 reflects the Houthi tanker-diversion effect in the Red Sea plus the Iran ceasefire fragility premium. The Ukraine strike on Bashneft did not yet visibly move WTI on 01 August, but the Ufa complex processes significant volumes of motor gasoline and aviation fuel destined for Russian military logistics. Any sustained supply disruption from the Ufa complex would tighten the Moscow-to-front fuel chain within weeks. [medium]

M2fred.stlouisfed.org at $23.155 trillion (June) is expanding at a modest pace. The Fed balance sheetfred.stlouisfed.org at $6.738 trillion continues its slow rundown via QT, now roughly $1.3 trillion below its 2022 peak. No TGA stress or repo market pressure signals in the current data.

United States politics and policy

The Treasury Department published a final rulefederalregister.gov eliminating disparate-impact liability from its Title VI Civil Rights Act regulations, aligning the department with a prior executive order and the narrower statutory text interpretation favored by the current administration. This follows a pattern of deregulatory Title VI rollbacks across multiple agencies and will affect federal grant compliance standards for Treasury counterparties, including state and local governments that receive Treasury-administered funds.

The Visa Bond Program was made permanent via final rulefederalregister.gov after a 12-month pilot launched August 2025. The program requires bond posting by applicants for temporary business/pleasure visas, a financial deterrent mechanism intended to reduce overstay rates. The FCC announced Auction 115federalregister.gov for 3,248 flexible-use licenses in the 3.98-4.14 GHz band, scheduled April 27, 2027. This upper C-band allocation is the next tranche of mid-band 5G capacity and will draw significant bids from all major US carriers.

The Michigan Supreme Court vacated a key permitironmountaindailynews.com for Enbridge's proposed Line 5 pipeline tunnel under the Straits of Mackinac, in a 6-1 decision. The court held that regulators failed to assess whether the tunnel extends the pipeline's operational life, thereby prolonging environmental harm to public trust resources. The decision remands the matter to the Michigan Public Service Commission and further clouds a project already in eight years of legal limbo. Tribal nations celebrated the ruling; Enbridge has not yet announced its next step. The Line 5 carry approximately 540,000 barrels per day of petroleum and NGLs between Superior, Wisconsin, and Sarnia, Ontario. Any shutdown scenario carries significant Great Lakes regional economic consequences. Michiganironmountaindailynews.com appeared in 7 cross-sections this week (conflict, foreign_news, gdelt_gkg, local_news, paper_bets, state_news, weather), making this a multi-vector story.

Notable court docket items: Advanced Energy United v. FERCcourtlistener.com (D.C. Circuit, 31 July) addresses clean energy grid access. Ralph de la Torre v. Bill Cassidycourtlistener.com (D.C. Circuit) involves the former Steward Health Care CEO, who was held in contempt of Congress last year. The Department of Energy logged renewed contract awards to all three major nuclear laboratory operators: Sandia National Laboratories (NTESS, $42.8B), Lawrence Livermore (LLNS, $41.5B), and Los Alamos (Triad, $35.1B).

Regional briefings

North America

The Michigan Line 5 tunnel permit decision (above) is the top domestic legal story. Separately, Canada logged government aircraft CFC4098 over Alaska airspace (64.66N, 161.45W) and CFC4073 transiting the Great Lakes region on 01 August, both consistent with northern patrol patterns. No anomalous government-aircraft convergences in the continental US data.

Germany's widening of deportations to Afghanistan is drawing US attention for its immigration enforcement template relevance. Germany deported the first Afghan national with no criminal record on 31 July; Faridoon Tofan, currently in deportation detention, fears the same fate. The US has observed Germany's policy shift closely as a potential precedent for its own removal programs.

The visa bond program now permanent (above). Alaska state legislative session produced 82 new state bill items, including the Susitna River power project development authorization and an LNG import facility regulatory framework.

South America

Thirteen people were killed when a small tourist aircraftdw.com crashed near the Nazca Lines geoglyphs in southern Peru on 01 August. The plane was carrying tourists on an overflights excursion. Peru's aviation regulator has launched an investigation. Fatal small-plane crashes at the Nazca Lines site have a history of inadequate safety enforcement. The crash brings renewed scrutiny to Peru's civil aviation oversight.

No significant EM debt or political events from the Andean bloc today. Brazil, Colombia, Venezuela, Argentina quiet in the current data cycle.

Europe

The Ceuta migration crisis escalated sharply this week. A Spanish Supreme Court ruling prevented at-sea pushbacks of migrants crossing from Morocco; within days, more than 70,000 peopleeuronews.com had crossed into the Spanish exclave, with Spain deploying army units to reinforce security. Italy suspended Schengen border-free movement with Spain in response, and Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez publicly accused EU partners of being "selfish" and "attacking" Spain from within. The EU Council of Interior Ministers will convene an emergency session. About 70,000 migrants have now voluntarily returned to Morocco over 48 hours, but the political and legal fracture within Schengen is structural: Italy and France are signaling willingness to treat this as a precedent for permanent intra-EU border controls. Belgian military aircraft JAF7XMopensky-network.org was spotted over the Ceuta-Morocco corridor (35.2N, 2.5W) at 5,539m on 01 August, and JAF9EGopensky-network.org transited the Strait of Gibraltar area.

Wildfires spread across Greece on 01-02 August, with an active fire near Porto Germeno on the Gulf of Corinth 60 km northwest of Athens forcing sea evacuations. French Premier stated fires in the Gironde are now under control, but conditions worsened again in Greece and parts of Spain. The entire Mediterranean arc is in a consecutive-heatwave summer; June 2026 was the hottest June ever recorded in Western Europe.

Germany's Pride events on 02 August saw large turnouts in Hamburg, Amsterdam, and Berlin, held one week after the Berlin Christopher Street Day attacken.wikipedia.org (25 July) in which a 21-year-old Lebanese-German man drove a van into the crowd and stabbed others, killing one woman and injuring 29. The suspect was shot dead by police the following day. He had received a suspended sentence in 2025 for ISIS affiliation planning. Interior Minister Dobrindt confirmed an Islamist terror investigation.

Lithuania will summonpravda.com.ua Russia's representative after the 01 August Kyiv ballistic strike damaged the Lithuanian embassy building in Kyiv.

Russia and post-Soviet

The Moscow restaurant bombingen.wikipedia.org on 01 August targeted the Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square. The device, a homemade IED with TNT-equivalent power and metal ball-bearing shrapnel, was packed into a gift box. The bomber, a woman, was stopped by a security guard at the entrance to a private banquet room and detonated the device on the restaurant's veranda; the guard, the bomber, and one customer died. Open-source reporting from Meduza and Baza connected the event to a birthday celebration for General Alexander Chaiko, commander of the Russian Aerospace Forces (VKS). Russian authorities confirmed terrorism investigation via the NAC; no group claimed responsibility. The non-attribution within 24 hours is notable given Russia's domestic intelligence apparatus.

Pavel Durov, founder of Telegram, was added by Russia's Rosfinmonitoring to the domestic terrorist-and-extremist registry on 30 July, the day after the FSB accused him of aiding terrorism by refusing to remove channels used by Ukrainian intelligence services and "extremist" groups. Telegram has approximately 90 million Russian users. Russian companies that maintain Telegram integrations began cutting ties within 48 hours of the designation. Durov responded publicly with a dismissive social media post. He holds French, UAE, and previous Russian citizenship and is based in Dubai, placing him outside Russia's immediate enforcement reach. The designation is primarily a blocking/freezing tool for domestic entities.

A Russian Rosguard officer in Khabarovsk beat a detainee who subsequently died; the Investigative Committee denied the two events were connected.

Iran warneddw.com Gulf neighbors on 01 August against assisting the United States in any capacity as Washington weighs further strikes. This followed Houthi claims of diverting multiple Saudi tankers from Red Sea transit. Sudan's civil war continued to draw coverage. Drone strikes on civilian infrastructure in the besieged city of el-Obeid in North Kordofan are hitting schools; aid organizations warn of a worsening humanitarian crisis in what has been called the world's worst food security emergency.

Africa

The DRC Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo viruswho.int is now the second-largest Ebola epidemic in recorded history, overtaking DRC's previous record with 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths as of 30 July (CFR 44%). WHO declared this a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) in May 2026. The outbreak has expanded from its origin in Ituri Province to five provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, Tshopo), now covering 49 health zones. Critically, Bundibugyo virus has no licensed vaccine and no approved therapeutic; this differentiates the outbreak from the Zaire-strain outbreaks where rVSV-ZEBOV-GP (Ervebo) and Inmazeb/mAb114 provided intervention options. The 44% case fatality ratio is below Zaire strain's historical 50-90% range but above the 2007 Bundibugyo outbreak's 25-36%. Uganda cases are also confirmed.

South and Southeast Asia

Mountaineer Nirmal Purja ("Nims"), 42, British-Nepalese, and nine other climbers were killed in an avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak (8,051m, world's 12th highest) on 01 August. Purja held the world record for summiting all 14 8,000m+ peaks in six months (2019), documented in the Netflix film "14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible." He was leading a commercial expedition when the avalanche struck at high altitude; Pakistani military search-and-rescue helicopters recovered four bodies and three were extracted in challenging weather. The other six climbers are presumed dead. Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region is in its prime climbing season but has experienced unusual late-July precipitation this year.

India's PM Modi released a video characterizing Citizenship Protest (CJP) demonstrators as "misguided children" who "deserve guidance," a gesture of political magnanimity consistent with his pre-election cycle posture after the protest movements.

A terrorist attack in Kulgam (Kashmir) killed at least one migrant laborer; the Resistance Front (TRF), a Lashkar-e-Taiba affiliate, is under investigation.

Ukraine theater (dedicated)

Anomaly

Resolution caveat: Frontline positions are reported to approximately 1 km precision from DeepStateMap community cartography. FIRMS thermal anomaly resolution is 375m. ACLED event precision is 1 km. Open sources do not support meter-level Russian unit position reporting; this section does not claim or imply it.

Ukraine theater maps for 2026-08-02 were not present in the briefings directory at publication time (cartographer pipeline may not have run yet for today). The maps from the previous cycle (2026-08-01) are referenced in the bundle.

Kyiv strike, 01 August: Russia launched 35 missiles (27 ballistic) and 185 attack drones at Ukraine overnight into 01 August. Only 2 missiles and 154 drones were intercepted. President Zelenskyy explicitly stated the cause: no interceptors remain for the Patriot system. Nine people were killed and 33 injured (including 4 children) in the Kyiv strike; 206 rescue workers responded. Five districts of Kyiv sustained damage to residential buildings and a supermarket. The Lithuanian embassy building in Kyiv was damaged; Vilnius will summon Russia's representative. The strike is Day 1,620 of full-scale invasion.

Strategic strikes deep into Russia: Simultaneously, Ukraine struck three Bashneft refineries in Ufa (Bashneft-Ufaneftekhim, Bashneft-Novoil, Bashneft-UNPZ), nearly 1,600 km from the front. Combined refining capacity exceeds 23 million metric tons/year; the facilities produce gasoline, diesel, aviation fuel, lubricants, and feedstocks directly relevant to Russian military logistics. The SBU confirmed the operation. Ukrainian naval drones sank the Rosatom-affiliated container ship Yanina (Fesco) 130 nautical miles from Novorossiysk in the Black Sea; Zelenskyy confirmed the ship was on OFAC/Western sanctions lists. All 17 crew were rescued. Ukraine also struck radar systems (4 confirmed by SBU).

Frontline operations: Ukrainian General Staff reported 193 Russian attacks repelled on 01 August, with the most intense combat on the Pokrovske (Donetsk direction) and Pivdenno-Slobozhanskyi (southern Kharkiv/Luhansk) directions. Russian glide bombs (KABs) struck central Kherson, killing one woman and injuring 18, damaging two hospitals. Dnipropetrovsk Oblast recorded two killed and 12 wounded in Russian strikes including teenagers.

FIRMS Ukraine sector: Multiple VIIRS thermal anomalies are logged in the 52.8-52.9N / 29.9-30.0E zone (Chernihiv/Kyiv area) overnight 31 July, with FRP values 0.86-1.71 MW. These are consistent with ground fire signatures, not industrial. A separate cluster in the 44.4-44.5N / 23.0-23.1E range (likely Transylvania/Romania given the coordinates) is consistent with summer agricultural burn rather than conflict.

Diplomacy: Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on 01 August that the US will "in the coming weeks" attempt to facilitate a resumption of direct Russia-Ukraine negotiations. The statement was vague on format and conditions. It followed Zelenskyy's call with the UAE President on Black Sea security and mutual cooperation projects.

Conflict and security signals

Ukraine recorded 9 confirmed fatalities in Kyiv and at least 3 additional in Kherson and Dnipropetrovsk on 01 August. Zelenskyy's 193 attacks repelled reflects the intensity of frontline contact, with Pokrovske and Pivdenno-Slobozhanskyi as the primary axes of Russian pressure. The Broad Peak avalanche killed 10 in a non-combat but high-visibility fatality event.

VIP flight tracking identified a US government aircraft NCR826 at (40.79N, 45.74W) at 11,582m and 829 km/h on 01 August. That coordinate places the aircraft near the Armenia-Azerbaijan-Georgia border region in the South Caucasus, consistent with monitoring of post-conflict stabilization activity or energy transit security. Belgian aircraft JAF7XM was over the Ceuta corridor at 5,539m, consistent with ISR support for the Spanish border crisis. US military C-17-class aircraft RCH646 (Memphis area) and RCH709 (UK overflight) are at routine logistics transit profiles.

Cyber and biosecurity

FIRST-OF-KIND KEV CALLOUT: CVE-2026-0770nvd.nist.gov targeting Langflow, the AI/LLM workflow orchestration framework, was added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerability catalog on 21 July with a remediation deadline of 24 July. This is the first agentic AI application framework ever added to the KEV catalog, representing a structural inflection point: the attack surface of AI-native infrastructure is now formally recognized as actively exploited in the wild, not merely theoretically vulnerable. The structural signal: as enterprises deploy Langflow and similar orchestration tools at scale for agentic workflows, the KEV designation means federal agencies and their contractors must patch or remove Langflow-dependent deployments immediately, and the private sector should treat this as a forcing function for AI supply-chain inventory.

The Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center hard-coded password vulnerability CVE-2026-20316nvd.nist.gov had a CISA remediation deadline of 01 August (today). Any federal agency using Cisco FMC that has not patched is now out of compliance. Fortinet FortiOS information-disclosure (CVE-2025-68686nvd.nist.gov, deadline 10 August), WordPress Core SQL injection (CVE-2026-60137nvd.nist.gov, deadline 04 August), and Microsoft SharePoint deserialization (CVE-2026-50522nvd.nist.gov) round out the active KEV window.

The Coldcard hardware wallet compromisethehackernews.com drained 1,196 Bitcoin addresses in 41 minutes on 30 July, extracting 1,082.65 BTC ($70.2 million). Galaxy Research mapped the sweep to a firmware flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard device. This is a supply-chain firmware attack on cryptographic hardware, a category that the broader financial security community has warned about for years. The attack surface is: wallet firmware update mechanisms that lack secure boot or code-signing verification.

Biosecurity: The DRC Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak (PHEIC, declared May 2026) has 3,605 cases and 1,587 deaths across 49 health zones in 5 provinces. No licensed vaccine. No approved therapeutic. WHO emergency response is active. ProMED data was absent from today's lake section output; supplemented by WebSearch. A WHO Emergency Use Listing process for experimental Bundibugyo-specific countermeasures appears to be underway but has not produced a licensed product. [high]

Humanitarian

The DRC Ebola response is the primary humanitarian emergency requiring attention. WHO has declared a PHEIC; international response capacity is constrained by active conflict in North and South Kivu (where the outbreak has spread) overlapping with the ongoing DRC civil conflict involving M23/Rwanda-backed forces. ReliefWeb data was absent from the current lake summary section output (section returned empty), suggesting ingest lag; supplemented by external sources. The 44% case fatality ratio, in the absence of a licensed vaccine, places a significant burden on case isolation, contact tracing, and supportive care capacity in areas with degraded health infrastructure.

Sudan's humanitarian deterioration continues in parallel. Aid organizations document drone strikes on school buildings in el-Obeid (North Kordofan), forcing school closures and population displacement in an area already facing acute food insecurity. The UN Sudan humanitarian response plan is chronically underfunded.

Environment, disasters, climate

Europe's wildfire emergency is the dominant environmental event. Greece is the current acute front, with fires burning near Porto Germeno (Gulf of Corinth, 60 km from Athens), forcing sea evacuations by residents escaping a wall of fire. A forest fire is also burning out of control in Bavaria, Germany. France's Gironde blaze is reported contained as of 02 August. The context: June 2026 was the hottest June ever recorded in Western Europe. A second major heat wave came in early July; the European health infrastructure recorded disproportionate female heat mortality relative to male, driven not primarily by biology but by age distribution, working conditions, and unequal access to air conditioning. Europe's low air-conditioning penetration rate (estimated 25-35% of households in southern Europe) leaves the elderly population particularly exposed.

No significant earthquakes above M5.0 appear in the current USGS or GDACS data for the 01 August cycle. GDACS did not flag any Orange or Red alerts in the current data window. FIRMS thermal anomalies in the ukraine_theater section are dominated by known battle-area and wildfire signatures.

The Broad Peak avalanche (see South & SE Asia above) occurred in Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan at high altitude; unusual late-July precipitation in the Karakoram range has been linked to climate-driven monsoon penetration into historically arid high-altitude zones.

Prediction markets and forecasting consensus

The Israel-Iran ceasefire is the most-traded geopolitical series in Polymarket this weekend. The daily resolution chain produces a precise term structure of failure probability:

  • Through 01 August: 99% YES, resolved (held)
  • Through 02 August: 78% YES ($1.1M volume), resolves tonight
  • Through 03 August: 70% YES ($301K volume), resolves Monday

The step-down implies 8-10 points per day of additional failure probability as of current market pricing. This is consistent with options-market-style theta: the market is pricing each day of ceasefire continuation as incrementally less certain, without a sharp discontinuity that would indicate a specific anticipated escalation event.

US invade Iran by end of 2026: 26% ($763K). This is the second-most-traded geopolitical market by volume, above Taiwan invasion ($324K at 1%). The 26% level is significantly elevated relative to base rates for superpower direct kinetic action against a nuclear-adjacent state in a five-month window; it reflects genuine uncertainty about whether the administration's "maximum pressure" posture includes a military component.

Trump insult Tucker Carlson by July 31: Resolved YES at 100% ($443K). This minor Polymarket bet resolved in the affirmative; Carlson and Trump publicly exchanged criticism in the prior week. The resolution is trivial in geopolitical terms but illustrates the breadth of Polymarket's coverage of domestic political behavior.

Weak signals - small things that may matter

The cross-section analysis for 01 August (the most recent complete day) surfaces the following high-confidence recurrences: California appears in 8 separate sections (foreign_news, local_news, paper_bets, sanctions_procurement, state_bills, state_news, ukraine_theater, weather) with 79 total mentions; Washington (state) appears in 7 sections (foreign_news, local_news, paper_bets, russian_internal, state_news, ukrainian_internal, weather) with 29 mentions; Ukraine appears in 6 sections (foreign_news, gdelt_gkg, paper_bets, russian_internal, ukraine_theater, ukrainian_internal) with 54 mentions. The California recurrence is the dominant cross-section signal.

The California cross-section warrants unpacking because it is unusual. California's 79 mentions spread across 8 sections, but the majority (60) come from state_bills, reflecting a legislative batch refresh. The substantively interesting co-occurrence is California appearing in both sanctions_procurement (a USASpending contract linked to a California entity) and ukraine_theater (a LiveUAMap event cited a California entity, possibly a defense contractor or NGO active in Ukraine reporting). The paper_bets mentions include a Kalshi earthquake probability market for California (KXEARTHQUAKECALIFORNIA-35) and a Mars rail project market, neither geopolitically urgent. The weather mentions cover active heat and fire alerts. Taken together, California's multi-section presence today is a volume artifact plus the sanctions_procurement-ukraine crosslink, which bears watching if it recurs.

The Durov/Telegram story is a structural weak signal of the highest order. Russia's designation of Durov as a terrorist simultaneously (a) makes Telegram's 90 million Russian users harder to reach through the platform, (b) creates compliance obligations for Russian firms that use Telegram for business communications, and (c) signals that the Kremlin is escalating pressure on encrypted communications precisely as the war enters a phase of intensified information operations. Telegram's channel infrastructure is a primary conduit for both Russian military bloggers (milbloggers) and Ukrainian frontline reporting; any degradation of Telegram's operational reliability inside Russia could paradoxically reduce the Kremlin's own battlefield-feedback channel. [medium]

The Adform ad-network compromise (tech_news, 01 August) deserves tracking: attackers modified a JavaScript file served by a global advertising technology company to rewrite cryptocurrency wallet addresses in browser sessions. Adform services large-scale publisher display advertising, meaning the attack surface was potentially millions of web sessions. The attack was contained by 01 August, but the category -- supply-chain compromise of ad-serving JavaScript to conduct financial theft -- is a novel delivery mechanism for crypto theft at scale. [medium]

Germany's pivot to deporting Afghans without criminal records is a policy weak signal. If this precedent holds, it reduces the effective asylum protection floor for Afghan nationals across the EU -- a signal to watch for Ireland, Sweden, and the Netherlands, which have their own pending policy reviews.
